$comment: Seed registry (Phase 0) — completed in Phase 4. Every narrative flag must be registered here before any map trigger or scene references it (CANON D-FLAG-01). Types: boolean | enum | counter. status: seed (canonical, incomplete refs) | test (tooling only) | final.

flags.description: The Chapter 1 macro-split (C-ROUTE-02). Set once at the Burning of Ulfheim; irreversible.
Phase 0 validator self-test flag; referenced only by the example map. Retire together with data/maps/example/.

The chapter's first grið: the raider boy (e6) at Longhouse Night yielded and Grím accepted. True = accepted (he lives, ransomed to the levy); false = refused/executed or the trigger never resolved. The tutorialized seed of C-ALIGN-05.

The ford peddler escaped east having seen the ambush chief's killing thrust inexplicably falter — the first Wyrd rumor is loose, as deniable luck ('the smith's boy the spears refuse'), per C-GRIM-05. False if he died or the battle went Unsung: nobody credible saw anything.
Grím stood at the truce-wand parley and Brandr named himself and his cause (C-LANDLESS-01). Gates name-barks in ch1-04 and the warmth of every later Landless encounter.

What survived Grove Road's witnesses: 'talked' = at least one neutral escaped after holding sightline (elev 2+, LoS) on the illegal blót — they WILL talk; 'unseen' = neutrals escaped but none ever saw the terrace; 'silenced' = every sighted unit died on the field. The Sung/Unsung lesson's permanent record (C-ALIGN-03/04).

The speak/silence choice before the king's clerk (Dag): did Grím name Þorgeir's blót to the crown? 'spoke' = testimony given (the grove is marked; Man-leaning); 'silent' = a thing seen and unsaid (the old kin-web sheltered; Blood-leaning). Only meaningful when grove_blot_witnessed != 'silenced' — dead witnesses leave nothing to attest.

How Bǫðvarr Bear-Sark's lawful yield was answered before a full house (always_sung). 'honored' = hand taken, wound-price accepted — the Bjarnholt seed planted; 'executed' = a yielded man killed at a lawful duel — guest-cup logic invoked, Bjarnholt enmity locked, and every hall sings it (C-ALIGN-05, C-CLAN-04 texture).

The unmasking beat: at the Yule feast the mask was torn away before the hall. What the firelight showed is deliberately NOT recorded in any flag, scene, or asset — the beat contradicts the sung burn-story without replacing it (C-GRIM-02, C-FRAME-02). The flag records only that it happened before witnesses.

The second níð has been recited: Grím is publicly named vargdropi, Aldís's whelp, before the Yule feast. The rumor the crown paid twenty years to close is a poem again (C-GRIM-03, C-KING-02). Always true after ch1-s08 — recorded as a flag because half the remaining game reads it.

While fugitive, Grím accepted Gunnhild's shelter (a fire, a meal, a banner half-offered) before the king's men took him. True changes every register of ch1-08 — the burning becomes guest-cup betrayal on top of kin-blood — and warms/chills Ch2 openings by route.

How many of the four Ulfheim households (n1-n4) exited the goat-track alive at the Burning, either route. 0-4. The number Ch2 keeps returning to: it is the count of voices that can counter-sing the crown's verse — or mourn yours.

Outlaw branch of the Burning: did the crown's recording skald (e13) escape the S edge? True = the crown's Ch2 hunt begins with facts (the king's memory lives); false = with rumor only (the detachment simply never came home). Read by the outlaw epilogue and Ch2-outlaw.
